newsitem.title: CHILE: Cervecerias sees $70 mln net in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Cervecerias sees $70 mln net in 1997.

text.p: Profits at Chile's largest brewery Cervecerias Unidas could rise to about $70 million this year from $43.4 million in 1996, Vice President Tomas Furst said.
"I think with the way we're going, we could reach about $70 million," he told Reuters.
First quarter profits showed a sharp increase, climbing about 38 percent to $29.9 million over the first quarter of 1996.

The brewery accounts for nearly 90 percent of Chilean domestic beer consumption and owns a controlling stake in one of the country's top wineries, Vina San Pedro, makers of the popular Gato brand. It also has a Pepsi bottling and distribution joint venture with Argentina's Baesa plus its owns beer investments in the Argentine provinces of Santa Fe and Salta.
Furst said the new shares from San Pedro's $15.8 million capital increase, approved by the winery's shareholders on June 2, will be placed on the local exchange by October.
"The board has approved it but the timetable is drawn out, October or September," he said.
CCU also owns 67 percent of a Croatian brewery, Karlovacka Pivovara, and is looking into building a brewery in the Bosnian capital of Sarajevo, company officials have said.
